decision: Report fleet LP lower bounds NOW for certified cells with an explicit bracket, instead of waiting for the lexicographic master. Demote the lexicographic work order below the initial-pool experiment.
rationale: Measured bus fixed cost is exactly 100000 while charging cost at the LP optimum is 86-2469 USD. For the combined-cost optimum x0 with route weight w and any minimum-fleet solution x*, 100000*w + C(x0) <= 100000*W* + C(x*) gives w - W* <= C(x*)/100000 <= ~0.025 at observed charging magnitudes. So the certified route weight brackets the true fleet LP bound to within about 0.03 buses. The lexicographic phase becomes a confirmation, not a blocker.
alternatives_rejected: (a) block all fleet claims until lexicographic CG exists -- rejected, the bracket is defensible and the data is in hand; (b) claim route_weight IS the fleet bound with no bracket -- rejected, that is the overclaim D0005 forbids

decision: MEASURED EXACTLY: at k02_s2 on the primary 15kWh/10min grid the fleet gap decomposes as 1 bus of route-space discretization plus 1 bus of column-pool composition. Both vanish at 1kWh/5min.
rationale: GIRO industrial fleet 2. Certified fleet LP bound 2.1875 (D0019). True discretized integer optimum 3, PROVEN by corrected branch-and-price (Phase I/II artificial certification, no Big-M pruning). Our CG pool plus one-shot MIP 4, proven optimal for that pool. Fine-grid 1kWh/5min pool MIP 2. So discretization costs exactly 1 (2->3) and pool composition exactly 1 more (3->4). Supersedes the earlier estimate of ~1 and ~2 buses.
alternatives_rejected: Estimating the split from the LP bound alone, which gave the wrong apportionment

decision: Column-pool composition is CONFIRMED as a real failure mode, so diversification, pool union and branch-and-price are attacking a genuine problem.
rationale: The open question was whether the pool MIP result of 4 at k02_s2 was already the model optimum (no pool failure) or whether the pool was deficient. Branch-and-price proves the model optimum is 3, so the pool is short by exactly one bus worth of complementary columns.
alternatives_rejected: Abandoning pool-enrichment work on the assumption that 4 was optimal

decision: CROSS-VALIDATED: the primary-grid integer optimum at k02_s2 is 3 buses, obtained independently by corrected branch-and-price and by a direct arc-flow MIP. All three primary k2 cells are 3/3/3. RAW pool excess is therefore 1/1/4 buses.
rationale: Two structurally different exact formulations agree. Branch-and-price proves 3 via Ryan-Foster with Phase I/II artificial certification; the arc-flow MIP solves the same discretized model directly with no column generation. GIRO achieves 2, so the primary 15kWh/10min grid costs exactly 1 bus at k2, confirmed twice.
alternatives_rejected: Relying on a single formulation for the model optimum

decision: Column generation provides NO bound-strength advantage for this model: the arc-flow LP equals the set-partitioning LP on all nine primary k2/k3/k5 cells (k02_s2 exactly 2.1875). CG's only possible justification is tractability at scale, which is now an open empirical question.
rationale: In this model a route IS a source-to-sink path in the SOC-by-time DAG -- SOC and time are network dimensions -- so by flow decomposition the two relaxations must coincide. This was predicted incorrectly by the manager, who told Agent C to expect a strictly weaker arc-flow bound; Agent C reported the equality honestly rather than 'fixing' a correct implementation.
alternatives_rejected: Assuming set partitioning is stronger, which holds only when route feasibility exceeds what the network encodes

decision: The RAW pool-composition failure (1/1/4 excess buses) is an artifact of the CG-then-one-shot-MIP pipeline, not of the model. Arc-flow has no pool and returns the true optimum directly. Pool enrichment is therefore only worth pursuing in the regime where arc-flow is intractable.
rationale: Arc-flow reached the proven optimum on all primary k2 cells with no pool at all, while the CG pool MIP overshot by 1/1/4 buses. Arc-flow's limit is size: k02_s1 fine-grid hit a 16.95M-arc LP and exceeded the local memory limit.
alternatives_rejected: Continuing to invest in diversification, pool union and branch-and-price without first locating the CG-versus-arc-flow crossover

decision: RETIRED: cross-resolution pool union does not repair primary-grid pool composition. My proposal of it was wrong.
rationale: Agent A executed it at k02_s2. primary_pool target 3 = INFEASIBLE (proof, not timeout) while the model optimum is 3 (D0025), so the pool is short exactly the 3-bus columns. The union's target-3 witness draws ONLY fine-grid routes and the fine pool alone reaches 2, so the union changes the route space rather than repairing the pool. Agent A also reports cross_resolution_cost_comparability=false: routes from different grids carry costs computed under different flooring conventions, so a mixed pool is not a valid instance of any stated model.
alternatives_rejected: (a) treating the union's target-2 result as a pool repair -- rejected, it is a different route space; (b) reporting a mixed-pool objective -- rejected, costs are not comparable across grids

decision: Both cheap pool-side levers are now retired, so the Goal-1 critical path reduces to one question: is a sufficiently fine representation affordable at scale?
rationale: Diversification saturates after 3 rounds and adds no further columns (B0022). Cross-resolution union changes the route space rather than repairing the pool (D0028). Remaining options are: run at a resolution where the pool suffices (1kWh/5min reaches GIRO's fleet, proven twice), branch-and-price on the coarse grid (validated but expensive, and only proves the coarse optimum of 3 which is worse than GIRO's 2), or an event-based representation. Only the resolution-cost study answers whether fine resolution scales.
alternatives_rejected: Further investment in pool enrichment before the CG-versus-arc-flow crossover is measured

decision: B0028 CLOSED: the arc-flow oracle enforces every one of 36 per-route constraints in exact_pricer_expanded.py, all network-encoded or objective-encoded. The LP equality therefore follows from flow decomposition and is not an artifact of a missing constraint.
rationale: Agent C produced a constraint-by-constraint audit. Two caveats do not affect the conclusion: --strict-tariff-coverage is input validation only and was not active in the baseline; and integer witnesses were found under a service-arc integrality relaxation, which is a search device that appears nowhere in the proof -- the lower bound comes from the certified LP (2.1875 implies integer >= 3) and the upper bound from a fully integral decomposition-verified witness at 3.
alternatives_rejected: Accepting the LP equality without auditing whether arc-flow was silently a relaxation
